cloud-security.label: Cloud Security
cloud-security.summary: Five-plus years across AWS, Azure, GCP and Microsoft 365 — from operating microservices platforms to securing regulated research data and governing cloud risk. I design the boundary, automate it, and keep the evidence that it held.

iam.label: Identity & Access
iam.summary: Five-plus years in cloud engineering and security, centred on who may reach what. I review access against least privilege, build workload identity with no reusable credential, and document every exception until it closes.

grc.label: Governance, Risk & Compliance
grc.summary: Five-plus years in cloud engineering and security, now focused on governance. I map controls to requirements, assess findings for business impact, and keep audit evidence that an assessor can trace from control to test to result.

devsecops.label: DevSecOps
devsecops.summary: Five-plus years building and securing cloud platforms — microservices on Kubernetes and OpenShift, infrastructure in Terraform, delivery through pipelines that fail when a control fails.

microsoft.label: Microsoft Cloud Security
microsoft.summary: Five-plus years across Azure and Microsoft 365 — infrastructure, Defender, data loss prevention, Intune and SCCM — with the controls, recovery and evidence that regulated environments require.

layers.title: Identity
layers.question: Who may enter.
layers.name: Identity & Access
layers.statement: Access is granted narrowly, reviewed on a schedule, and never stored as a secret.
layers.scene: Only verified identities pass the gate. Everything else stops before it reaches the network.

work.text: Review identity and access assignments against least privilege, document exceptions, and run periodic access reviews with system owners.
Built workload identity with no reusable credential: a managed identity scoped to a single secret, with a decoy secret that proves the boundary by returning 403.
Removed stored secrets from delivery with GitHub OIDC; an ABAC condition limits the one role the pipeline may grant.

layers.title: Network
layers.question: Where it may go.
layers.name: Boundary & Configuration
layers.statement: Boundaries default to deny, and configuration is held to a baseline.
layers.scene: Four subnets and no route out. Quarantine can only talk to the sensors.

work.text: Review compute, network and storage configuration against security baselines and carry each misconfiguration through remediation with its infrastructure owner.
Designed, deployed and hardened Azure infrastructure — virtual machines, networking and storage — while reducing cost by 15%.
Designed AWS architectures across EC2, EKS, VPC, S3 and RDS.
Built a sealed AWS range with no internet or NAT path, no public addresses and a quarantine subnet, gated by guardrail tests before any workload exists.

layers.title: Workload
layers.question: What it may run.
layers.name: Platform & Delivery
layers.statement: Platforms are built as code and delivered by pipelines that are themselves controls.
layers.scene: Probed from inside the workload: one action allowed, seven denied.

work.text: Led a six-engineer team operating 30+ microservices through deployment, migration, maintenance and troubleshooting.
Migrated microservices from Linux hosts to OpenShift, and from OpenShift to AWS.
Automated infrastructure with Terraform and PowerShell, cutting manual effort by 40%.
Automated Azure deployment with PowerShell and JSON templates, cutting manual effort by 30%.
Made the pipeline block on security: Bicep lint with security rules as errors, Checkov, Gitleaks across full history, and traceability tests.

layers.title: Data
layers.question: What it may read.
layers.name: Data & Endpoint
layers.statement: Sensitive data stays classified and contained, on devices that are patched and compliant.
layers.scene: One identity, one secret, one network path to it.

work.text: Designed security for regulated research data, improving secure workload onboarding by 30%.
Configured data loss prevention and threat-management policy in the Microsoft Security & Compliance Center.
Administered Microsoft 365 — Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Teams and Defender — improving platform reliability by 20%.
Ran SCCM and Intune across 500+ devices: deployment, patching, compliance enforcement and device policy.

layers.title: Detection
layers.question: What we will see.
layers.name: Risk, Detection & Response
layers.statement: Find the weakness before an attacker does; see the attempt when one comes.
layers.scene: Every read, denial and permission change is logged and alerted.

work.text: Reduced high-risk misconfiguration exposure by 25% through vulnerability testing, risk analysis and security assessment of cloud infrastructure.
Assess vulnerability and configuration findings for risk and business impact, and track corrective action through validation and closure.
Monitored cloud environments for threats and supported incident response, improving response turnaround by 20%.
Hardened cloud infrastructure and responded to security incidents alongside IT security.
Threat-modelled with STRIDE and ran eight adversary-emulation scenarios; each finding was fixed and re-tested or formally risk-accepted.

layers.title: Evidence
layers.question: Proof that it held.
layers.name: Governance & Resilience
layers.statement: Controls are mapped to requirements, tested, and recoverable — with evidence an assessor can trace.
layers.scene: Controls mapped to tests, tests to evidence, evidence hashed.

work.text: Map cloud controls to policy and compliance requirements, identify gaps, and maintain risk records and audit evidence through remediation.
Defined security requirements and control mappings, increasing documented control coverage by 35%.
Wrote security standards, runbooks and continuity and recovery procedures, improving audit readiness and resilience by 30%.
Integrated cloud services across IT, development, research and infrastructure teams, reducing security-review delays by 25%.
Delivered backup and disaster recovery for Azure resources and SQL databases, holding 99.9% data availability.
Traced 29 NIST SP 800-53 controls from implementation to test, evidence and threat, with tests that fail the build when a threat loses its control.
